summary: Three independent fresh-context Opus reviews over the two library features added after the enrichment work (a mis-typed-library report, and a library retype that purges catalog rows). The first two returned FIX-FIRST with three highs each; this one returned LOWS-ONLY — no critical, no high, 3 medium, 8 low. It mutation-verified all nine earlier fixes independently (watcher re-point, transitive cascade closure, casualty nouns, install-line scoping, mid-scan exclusion, RowsAffected belt, scan-slot claim/release, typed-nil narrowing, expected_items pointer) and measured the preview against reality: seeded rows across the cascade closure, ran the retype, and the preview matched actual deletions exactly on 18 tables, including correctly NOT counting the SET NULL case. Both drift guards demonstrated firing against real probe tables. Fixed after that verdict: dropping the stale watch on a WatchLibrary failure also dropped the library out of PERIODIC scanning (w.watching is what periodicScanLoop iterates; a review measured a 60ms tick firing nothing after an unwatch), so the entry is now installed anyway with the current value and the call returns ErrFSWatchUnavailable; the purge transaction ran on the request context under a 60s route timeout, where a cancellation racing Commit answers 500 with no rescan launched while the purge may have landed; two post-retype assertions counted catalog-wide and blamed production code for test pollution; WatchedLibrary's COPY was shallow so Paths aliased the live snapshot; the re-point ORDERING was unpinned because an empty tree rescans in milliseconds and the test polled for the final state; libraryIsStarved omitted the mid-scan exclusion it claims to mirror; and a library deleted mid-retype got re-watched by the goroutine. NOTE the reviewed sha was a5cc5ba (pre-rebase) and this record is against a later tip: the delta is those fixes, each re-verified by the reviewer's own mutations, but not itself re-reviewed; the branch was also rebased onto main after PR #515 merged, with an identical tree. Recorded rather than fixed and in CLAUDE.md: FOR UPDATE is pinned by nothing (a plain SELECT passes every test; the outcome stays safe only because RowsAffected turns an over-delete into a 409); the preview enumerates deletions so both SET NULL side effects go unreported; live watch parties are deleted underneath internal/watchparty's in-memory manager; the rescan goroutine is a bare go like Create's and Scan's. Earlier rounds found and closed, each demonstrated by running code: the next scan silently undoing a retype via the watcher's stale library snapshot; the preview omitting every transitive cascade including a person's whole recap Q&A thread; casualty descriptions borrowed from the merge's prose telling an admin a live watch party would be re-parented; a mid-scan library flipping the whole report to check-your-TMDB-key and silencing the real warning beside it; and three fixes pinned by no test at all.
